title: Democrats Sue Pentagon Over Emergency Changes to Overseas Voting Forms
snippet: The Democratic National Committee has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration after the Pentagon used an emergency measure to alter voter registration forms for Americans living abroad.
content:
WASHINGTON — The Democratic National Committee has launched a legal challenge against the Pentagon and the Office of Management and Budget, alleging that the administration improperly used emergency measures to alter federal voter registration forms for military service members and civilian Americans living overseas.

Voting rights advocates and Democratic officials argue the sudden rule change is a calculated effort to suppress the overseas vote ahead of high-stakes midterm elections. More than 2 million American citizens living outside the U.S. are currently eligible to cast ballots in domestic elections.

Key Alterations to the Overseas Ballot Form

The changes impact the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), a standardized document used by overseas voters to register and request absentee ballots. The updated version introduces stricter identification requirements and removes a specific option that allowed individuals to indicate they are U.S. citizens who have never lived in the United States.

This category, often referred to as "never resideds," includes adult children of American citizens born or raised abroad. Currently, 37 states permit these individuals to vote using their parents' previous U.S. residency. Under the new guidelines, affected voters can no longer use the simplified federal form and must navigate state-specific registration processes instead.

Furthermore, updated federal website guidance now claims the form is intended solely for citizens who plan to return to the U.S., adding a limitation that previously did not exist.

Dispute Over 'Emergency' Justification

To implement the modifications without the standard public comment period, the Department of Defense sought expedited approval from OMB in August. Deputy Undersecretary of War for Personnel and Readiness Sean O’Keefe argued in a letter that the previous document caused confusion about eligibility and that standard rulemaking procedures could not be completed with less than 90 days before the federal election.

However, election experts have publicly questioned the administration's rationale, emphasizing that federal elections are scheduled years in advance and no operational crisis had been reported by state officials.

"I don’t think there is an actual emergency," said Tammy Patrick, chief program officer at the National Association of Election Officials, adding that election workers nationwide had raised no infrastructure concerns that would warrant an expedited overhaul.

High Political Stakes Ahead of Midterms

The lawsuit comes as both parties prepare for tightly contested midterm races, with control of the House of Representatives hanging in the balance. Democratic leaders contend the administration manufactured a procedural emergency to disenfranchise voters living abroad.

Advocacy groups have warned that the changes will lead to widespread confusion among both voters and local election clerks.

"The result will be confusion, chaos and fewer overseas votes," warned Doris Speer, president of the Association of Americans Resident Overseas. Meanwhile, voter engagement groups like the U.S. Vote Foundation confirmed they are examining additional legal avenues to challenge the administration's actions in court.
